blocks.text: Assalam o alaikum bachon! Pichle sabaq (7.1.4) mein humne displacement-time graph dekha tha, jahan graph ki oonchai particle ki position batati thi. Aaj hum ek naya graph parhenge: velocity-time graph. Is graph mein oonchai position nahin balke velocity (raftaar aur simt dono) batati hai. Yeh graph physics aur mathematics dono ke exam mein bohat aata hai, aur is ki do baatein hamesha yaad rakhni hain: slope (dhalaan) se acceleration milta hai aur area (raqba) se displacement. Aaj hum dono baaton ki wajah bhi samjhenge, sirf ratta nahin lagayenge. Sabaq ke aakhir mein do kitabi misaalein (Example 5 aur 6) hal karenge: ek mein cyclist ka displacement aur deceleration, aur doosri mein Ali ki gaari ki shuru wali raftaar. Har qadam par hum yeh bhi poochenge ke yeh qadam kyun uthaya, taa ke aap naye sawal mein khud faisla kar sakein ke kaun sa tareeqa lagana hai.
Kitab kehti hai ke velocity-time graph hamein nazar se (visually) samjhata hai ke kisi cheez ki velocity waqt ke saath kaise badal rahi hai. Is graph ko in kaamon ke liye use kiya jata hai:

items: Uniform (yaksaan) ya non-uniform (ghair yaksaan) motion ko samajhna
Mukhtalif time intervals (waqt ke hisson) mein motion ko saaf aur achhi tarah study karna

blocks.text: Velocity-time graph mein velocity (\(v\)) ko \(y\)-axis (khari line) par aur time (\(t\)) ko \(x\)-axis (leti hui line) par plot kiya jata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Sab se pehle ek ghalti se bachiye jo bohat se students karte hain: velocity-time graph ko displacement-time graph samajh lena. Dono dekhne mein milte julte hain lekin matlab bilkul alag hai.
Displacement-time graph mein oonchai = position \(x\), aur slope = velocity.
Velocity-time graph mein oonchai = velocity \(v\), slope = acceleration, aur graph ke neeche ka area = displacement.
Misal ke taur par agar velocity-time graph ek leti hui seedhi line ho to is ka matlab hai ke particle ek hi raftaar se chal raha hai, ruka hua nahin. Ruka hua particle tab hoga jab line bilkul \(t\)-axis par ho, yani \(v = 0\).
Key Features of Velocity-Time Graph
1. Graph ka slope \(\left(\frac{dv}{dt}\right)\) particle ka acceleration batata hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Ab sawal yeh hai ke slope hi acceleration kyun hai? Kisi seedhi line ka slope hota hai \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}\), yani oopar kitna gaye taqseem aage kitna gaye. Velocity-time graph mein "oopar jana" velocity ka badalna hai (\(\Delta v\)) aur "aage jana" waqt ka guzarna hai (\(\Delta t\)). To slope \(= \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}\), aur 7.1.3 mein humne parha tha ke velocity mein tabdeeli taqseem waqt hi acceleration hai. Agar graph curve ho to kisi point par tangent (woh line jo curve ko us point par sirf chhooti hai) ka slope \(\frac{dv}{dt}\) hota hai, jo us lamhe ka acceleration hai.
Units bhi axes se hi aate hain: (m/s) har second mein, yani m/s\(^2\).
• Agar particle constant (na badalne wale) acceleration se chal raha ho to us ka velocity-time graph seedhi line hota hai.

items: Agar \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 0\) ho to velocity-time graph ek horizontal (leti hui) seedhi line hota hai. Figure 7.4 mein point \(B\) se point \(C\) tak particle uniform velocity se chal raha hai. Velocity badal nahin rahi, is liye line na oopar jati hai na neeche.

Agar \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \text{constant} > 0\) ho to particle ki velocity waqt ke saath barhti jati hai, aur graph oopar chadhti hui seedhi line hota hai. Figure 7.4 mein point \(A\) se point \(B\) tak particle positive uniform acceleration se chal raha hai.

Agar \(a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \text{constant} < 0\) ho to particle ki velocity waqt ke saath kam hoti jati hai, aur graph neeche girti hui seedhi line hota hai. Figure 7.4 mein point \(C\) se point \(D\) tak particle uniform negative acceleration (retardation, yani raftaar ka dheema hona) se chal raha hai.

blocks.alt: Velocity-time graph with v on the vertical axis and t on the horizontal axis. A straight line rises from A to B (labelled a > 0), stays horizontal from B to C (labelled a = 0), then falls from C to D (labelled a < 0).
blocks.caption: Figure 7.4: velocity-time graph with uniform acceleration (A to B), uniform velocity (B to C) and uniform retardation (C to D) (original drawing after the textbook's figure; axis and BC labels corrected)

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Figure 7.4 velocity-time graph hai, lekin kitab ne is ke vertical axis par \(x\) likh diya hai aur BC wale hisse par "\(v = 0\)" likha hai. Yeh dono cheezein Figure 7.1 (displacement-time graph) se copy ho gayi hain. Sahi yeh hai: vertical axis \(v\) hai, aur BC par velocity zero nahin balke constant hai, is liye wahan \(a = 0\) likha hona chahiye. Kitab ka apna text bhi yahi kehta hai ke \(B\) se \(C\) tak particle uniform velocity se chal raha hai. Hamari drawing mein sahi labels lage hain.

blocks.title: Recall!
blocks.text:
• Displacement = Area under velocity-time graph
• Acceleration = Slope of velocity time graph

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Ek bus stop se chalti hai, raftaar pakadti hai, kuch der ek hi raftaar se chalti hai, phir agle stop par ruk jati hai. Is ka velocity-time graph kis shakal ka hoga?
Jawab: bilkul Figure 7.4 jaisa, lekin aakhir mein line \(t\)-axis tak aayegi kyun ke bus ruk gayi (\(v = 0\)). Pehla hissa oopar chadhti line (\(a > 0\)), beech mein leti line (\(a = 0\)), aakhir mein girti line (\(a < 0\)).
• Agar particle variable (badalte hue) acceleration se chal raha ho to us ka velocity-time graph seedhi line nahin hota. (Figure 7.5 dekhiye)

blocks.alt: Velocity-time graph drawn as a smooth curve that rises to a peak and then falls, showing variable acceleration.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.5: a curved velocity-time graph, variable acceleration (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Seedhi line ka slope har jagah ek jaisa hota hai. Is liye seedha velocity-time graph ka matlab hai ke har lamhe acceleration ek hi hai. Figure 7.5 mein curve pehle tezi se oopar jata hai, phir dheere dheere kam dhalwaan hota hai, choti par bilkul flat ho jata hai (us ek lamhe acceleration zero hai), aur phir neeche aane lagta hai (acceleration negative). Yani acceleration lagataar badal raha hai, isi liye graph mud jata hai.
Dhyan dein: aisi motion mein 7.1.6 wali teen equations of motion kaam nahin karti, kyun ke woh sirf constant acceleration ke liye hain. Wahan hum calculus (differentiation aur integration) use karte hain.

2. Ab doosri aur sab se ahem baat. Agar \(A\) woh area ho jo velocity-time graph ke neeche aur time-axis ke oopar, \(t = t_{1}\) se \(t = t_{2}\) tak hai, to integral calculus se:
\[A = \int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} v(t)\,dt\]
Chun ke \(v = \frac{dx}{dt}\) hai (velocity position ka rate of change hai), is liye:
\[A = \int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} \dfrac{dx}{dt}\,dt\]
\[= \int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} dx\]
\[= x(t_{2}) - x(t_{1})\]
Is tarah \(A\) = waqt \(t_{1}\) se \(t_{2}\) tak particle ka displacement. Yani graph ke neeche ka area hi displacement hai.

blocks.title: Recall!
blocks.text: If \(y = f(x) \ge 0\) for \(a \le x \le b\), then the area under the curve \(y = f(x)\), above the \(x\)-axis, and between the vertical lines \(x = a\), \(x = b\) is equal to \(\int_{a}^{b} y\,dx\).

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Is baat ko sab se aasan misaal se samajhte hain. Ek gaari 5 second tak barabar 20 m/s ki raftaar se chalti hai. Us ka graph 20 ki oonchai par ek leti line hai, aur us ke neeche ek rectangle (mustateel) banta hai jis ka area \(20 \times 5 = 100\) hai. Ab socho, gaari ne kitna faasla tay kiya? Raftaar \(\times\) waqt \(= 20 \times 5 = 100\) m. Dono jawab ek hi hain! Yani "velocity \(\times\) time" hi graph ke neeche ka area hai.
Jab velocity badalti rahe to hum waqt ko bohat patli patli strips (pattiyon) mein kaat dete hain. Har patti mein velocity taqreeban constant hoti hai, is liye har patti ka area us chhote se waqt mein tay hone wala faasla hai. Sab pattiyon ko jama karna hi integral \(\int v\,dt\) ka kaam hai. Aakhri qadam Fundamental Theorem se aata hai: kisi cheez ke rate ko integrate karein to us cheez ki kul tabdeeli mil jati hai, yani \(x(t_{2}) - x(t_{1})\).

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text:
Agar velocity-time graph time axis ke oopar bhi ho aur neeche bhi, aur \(A_{1}\) woh area ho jo time axis aur graph ke darmiyan axis ke oopar hai, jab ke \(A_{2}\) woh area ho jo axis ke neeche hai, to:
\[\text{Displacement} = A_{1} - A_{2}\]
\[\text{Distance} = A_{1} + A_{2}\]

blocks.alt: Velocity-time curve shaped like a wave that crosses the t-axis. Between two vertical lines, the region above the t-axis and under the curve is shaded and labelled A1; the region below the t-axis and above the curve is shaded and labelled A2.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.6: area A1 above the time axis and area A2 below it (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yeh minus kyun aur plus kyun? Axis ke neeche velocity negative hai, yani particle ulti simt mein (peeche ki taraf) chal raha hai. Ghar se 12 m aage jao aur phir 5 m wapas aao: displacement (shuru se aakhir tak seedha faasla) \(12 - 5 = 7\) m hai, lekin chale kitna? \(12 + 5 = 17\) m. Displacement mein peeche jana aage jane ko kaat deta hai, is liye \(A_{2}\) minus hota hai. Distance mein har qadam ginti mein aata hai, is liye plus.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(A_{1}\) aur \(A_{2}\) dono positive numbers maane gaye hain. Agar aap seedha poore waqfe ka integral \(\int v\,dt\) lein to axis ke neeche wala hissa khud hi negative aa jata hai aur jawab seedha \(A_{1} - A_{2}\) aata hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Figure 7.6 ko ghor se dekhiye. Pehli khari line se le kar us jagah tak jahan curve axis ko kaatta hai, velocity positive hai: particle aage ja raha hai. Us ke baad doosri khari line tak velocity negative hai: particle wapas aa raha hai. Ab sochiye: jis lamhe curve axis ko kaatta hai, us waqt particle kya kar raha hota hai?
Jawab: us ek lamhe \(v = 0\) hai, yani particle pal bhar ke liye ruk kar simt badalta hai, bilkul jaise oopar phenki gayi gaind choti par ek pal ruk kar wapas girti hai. Agar \(A_{1} = 12\) aur \(A_{2} = 5\) hon to displacement \(12 - 5 = 7\) aur distance \(12 + 5 = 17\) hoga. Aur agar \(A_{1} = A_{2}\) ho to displacement zero, yani particle wahin wapas aa gaya jahan se chala tha, halaan ke distance zero nahin.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Ek aur baat jo exam mein kaam aati hai: graph ke neeche ka area hamesha "oonchai ki unit \(\times\) chaurai ki unit" mein hota hai. Agar velocity km/h mein ho aur time hours mein, to area km mein aayega. Agar velocity m/min mein aur time minutes mein, to area meter mein. Is liye sawal shuru karne se pehle dono axes ki units zaroor dekh lein. Agar ek axis par seconds aur doosre par km/h ho to pehle units ko ek jaisa karna parega, warna jawab ghalat aayega. Aur yaad rakhein ke slope ki unit "oonchai ki unit taqseem chaurai ki unit" hoti hai, jaise m/min taqseem min = m/min\(^2\).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh misaal kitab ki nahin, hamari taraf se hai.) Ek motorcycle 4 second tak 10 m/s ki barabar raftaar se chalti hai, phir yaksaan tareeqe se dheemi ho kar agle 2 second mein ruk jati hai. Kul displacement aur aakhri 2 second ka acceleration nikaalein.
Graph: 0 se 4 tak 10 ki oonchai par leti line, phir 4 se 6 tak girti line jo \(t = 6\) par axis ko chhooti hai.
Area = rectangle + triangle:
\[10 \times 4 + \tfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 10 = 40 + 10 = 50 \text{ m}\]
Acceleration = girti line ka slope:
\[a = \dfrac{0 - 10}{6 - 4} = -5 \text{ m/s}^{2}\]
Yani motorcycle ne 50 m displacement kiya aur aakhir mein 5 m/s\(^2\) ki retardation thi.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Graph wale sawalon mein yeh tarteeb rakhein: sab se pehle axes ki units parhein (minutes hain ya hours, m/min hai ya km/h). Phir graph ke neeche wale hisse ko rectangles, triangles aur trapeziums mein todein. Acceleration ke liye slope, displacement ke liye area. Aur units kabhi mix na karein: m/min ko min se zarb dein to m milta hai.

blocks.alt: Velocity-time graph with v from 0 to 6 and t from 0 to 12. Horizontal line from A(0, 6) to B(8, 6), then a straight line down to C(12, 0). A dashed vertical line joins B to D(8, 0). O is the origin.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.7: velocity-time graph of the cyclist in Example 5 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Example 5
blocks.problem:
Figure 7.7 is the velocity-time graph for a cyclist traveling in a straight line. (The time is in minutes and velocity is in meters per minute).
(a) Calculate the total displacement of the cyclist from his starting position at the end of the 12 minutes.
(b) Determine the uniform deceleration during the final 4 minutes of motion.
steps:
Diya gaya: Figure 7.7 ka velocity-time graph. \(t = 0\) se \(t = 8\) min tak velocity 6 m/min hai (AB hissa), phir yaksaan tareeqe se kam ho kar \(t = 12\) min par 0 ho jati hai (BC hissa).
Maloom karna: (a) 12 minute mein kul displacement; (b) aakhri 4 minute mein uniform deceleration (raftaar ka yaksaan kam hona).
Tareeqa: sab se pehle socho ke graph se displacement kaise milta hai: graph ke neeche ka area. Aur acceleration: graph ka slope. Graph ke neeche ki shakal trapezium OABC hai (char kono wali shakal jis ki do sides parallel hain), to hum us ka area nikaalenge. Phir (b) ke liye BC ka slope.

Hal (a): area ki equation banayein
Maan lijiye \(x\) kul displacement hai. Displacement graph ke neeche ke area ke barabar hai, jo trapezium OABC ka area hai:
\[x = \text{Area of trapezium } OABC\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(a + b)h \quad \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: AB aur OC dono leti hui lines hain, is liye yahi parallel sides ka joda hain. OA dono par perpendicular (amood) hai, is liye wahi height hai. Trapezium ka formula neeche "Area of Trapezium" box mein diya hai.

\(a\), \(b\), \(h\) pehchaanein
\(a\) = neeche wali side \(\overline{OC} = 12\),
\(b\) = oopar wali side \(\overline{AB} = 8\),
\(h\) = \(\overline{OC}\) aur \(\overline{AB}\) ke darmiyan oonchai \(= 6\).
Kyun: O \(t = 0\) par aur C \(t = 12\) par hai, to OC ki lambai 12 hai. A \(t = 0\) par aur B \(t = 8\) par hai, to AB ki lambai 8. Oonchai velocity ki value 6 m/min hai.
Dhyan dein: bohat se bachay \(b = 12 - 8 = 4\) le lete hain. Nahin! AB poori oopar wali side hai, 0 se 8 tak.

Equation (1) mein values rakhein
\[x = \dfrac{1}{2}(12 + 8) \times 6\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 6\]
\[= 60 \text{ meters}\]
Kyun: units ka hisaab: (m/min) \(\times\) (min) \(=\) m. Minute cancel ho jate hain aur meter bachte hain, jo displacement ki sahi unit hai.

Hal (b): BC ka slope
Maan lijiye \(a\) aakhri 4 minute ka acceleration hai, to:
\[a = \text{slope of } \overline{BC}\]
\[= \dfrac{0 - 6}{12 - 8}\]
\[= -\dfrac{6}{4} = -\dfrac{3}{2} \text{ m/min}^{2}\]
Kyun: B(8, 6) se C(12, 0) tak velocity mein tabdeeli \(0 - 6 = -6\) aur waqt \(12 - 8 = 4\) hai; slope \(= \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}\) hi acceleration hai. Minus ka matlab hai ke velocity kam ho rahi hai, yani \(\frac{3}{2}\) m/min\(^2\) ki deceleration.

Tasdeeq:
OABC ko rectangle OABD aur triangle BDC mein todein:
\[8 \times 6 + \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 6 = 48 + 12 = 60\]
Wahi 60 aaya. Aur \(a = -\frac{3}{2}\) se 4 minute mein velocity \(\frac{3}{2} \times 4 = 6\) kam hoti hai, 6 se 0, bilkul jaise graph dikhata hai.
blocks.answer: (a) Total displacement \(x = 60\) m. (b) \(a = -\frac{3}{2}\) m/min\(^2\), i.e. a uniform deceleration of \(\frac{3}{2} = 1.5\) m/min\(^2\).

blocks.title: Area of Trapezium
blocks.text:
A trapezium (trapezoid) is a four-sided plane figure that has exactly one pair of parallel sides. If \(a\) and \(b\) are the lengths of parallel sides and \(h\) is the perpendicular distance between them, then the area is given by:
\[\text{Area} = \dfrac{1}{2}(a + b) \times h\]

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
Example 5 mein agar cyclist 8 minute ke bajaye 10 minute tak 6 m/min se chalta aur phir 2 minute mein rukta, to displacement kitna hota?
Jawab: \(\frac{1}{2}(12 + 10) \times 6 = 66\) m. Lekin deceleration ab \(\frac{6}{2} = 3\) m/min\(^2\) hoti, yani jaldi rukne ke liye zyada zor se brake lagana parta. Is se ek aam qaida samajh aata hai: velocity-time graph mein jitni zyada dhalwaan (steep) girti line, utni zyada retardation. Aur jitna bara area, utna zyada displacement. Slope aur area do alag sawalon ke jawab hain, in ko kabhi aapas mein mix na karein. Exam mein pehle khud se poochiye: "mujh se rate poocha gaya hai ya kul miqdaar?" Rate ho to slope, kul miqdaar ho to area.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Example 6 se pehle ek zaroori baat. Ab tak hum graph se seedha jawab nikaal rahe the: area nikala, displacement mil gaya. Example 6 mein ulta kaam hai: displacement (400 km) humein diya gaya hai, aur graph ki ek oonchai \(u\) maloom nahin. Aise sawalon ka tareeqa yeh hai: maloom na hone wali cheez ko ek letter (yahan \(u\)) maan lo, poora area usi letter ki shakal mein likho, aur phir use di gayi value ke barabar rakh do. Is tarah ek seedhi si linear equation (pehle darje ki equation) ban jati hai jise hal karna aasan hai.
Ek aur baat: kitab ne Figure 7.8 ko "sketch" kaha hai, yani yeh scale par bani hui nahin. Is liye lambaiyan graph se naap kar nahin, balke sawal mein di gayi values se lein.

blocks.alt: Velocity-time sketch. The line starts at A(0, u) on the v-axis, rises to B(3, 70), stays level to C(6, 70), then drops to D(6.5, 0) on the t-axis. Dotted lines: from B down to E(3, 0), from A across to F(3, u), from the 70 mark across to B, and from C down to t = 6. O is the origin.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.8: velocity-time sketch of Ali's drive in Example 6 (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Example 6
blocks.problem:
Ali drives a car 400 km in a straight line. Figure 7.8 is a sketch of a velocity-time graph representing his motion. Ali starts with a velocity of \(u\) km/h and accelerates to a velocity of 70 km/h in 3 hours. He then maintains his velocity for 3 hours, after which he slows down uniformly to rest over the next \(\frac{1}{2}\) hour. Find:
(a) The value of \(u\)
(b) The acceleration of Ali during the first 3 hours of his drive.
steps:
Diya gaya: kul displacement 400 km; pehle 3 ghante mein velocity \(u\) se yaksaan barh kar 70 km/h hoti hai (A se B); phir \(t = 3\) se \(t = 6\) ghante tak 70 km/h rehti hai (B se C); phir agle aadhe ghante mein yaksaan kam ho kar \(t = 6.5\) par zero ho jati hai (C se D).
Maloom karna: (a) \(u\) ki value; (b) pehle 3 ghante ka acceleration.
Tareeqa: yahan \(u\) maloom nahin, lekin kul displacement maloom hai. Graph ke neeche ka area = displacement = 400. Area ko \(u\) ki shakal mein likh kar 400 ke barabar rakhein to \(u\) ki equation ban jayegi. Phir (b) mein AB ka slope.

Hal (a): area ko do hisson mein todein
Chun ke displacement graph ke neeche ka area hai:
\[x = \text{area of } OABE + \text{area of } BCDE\]
\[x = \tfrac{1}{2}(a + b) h_{1} + \tfrac{1}{2}(c + d) h_{2}\ \text{...(1)}\]
Kyun: \(t = 3\) par dotted line BE poore area ko do trapeziums mein kaat deti hai. OABE mein parallel sides OA aur BE khari (vertical) hain; BCDE mein parallel sides BC aur ED leti (horizontal) hain.

Lambaiyan pehchaanein
\(a = |OA| = u\), \(b = |BE| = 70\), \(h_{1} = |OE| = 3\)
\(c = |BC| = 6 - 3 = 3\), \(d = |ED| = 6.5 - 3 = 3.5\), \(h_{2} = b = 70\)
Kyun: OABE mein parallel sides khari hain, to un ke darmiyan faasla leta hua \(OE = 3\) hai. BCDE mein parallel sides leti hain, to un ke darmiyan faasla khara 70 hai.
Dhyan dein: BCDE ki height 70 hai, 0.5 nahin. Height hamesha do parallel sides ke darmiyan ka perpendicular faasla hoti hai.

Equation (1) mein values rakhein
\[x = \tfrac{1}{2}(u + 70)\times 3 + \tfrac{1}{2}(3 + 3.5)\times 70\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(3u + 210 + 455)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{2}(3u + 665)\]
Kyun: \((u + 70) \times 3 = 3u + 210\) aur \(6.5 \times 70 = 455\). Dono hisson mein \(\frac{1}{2}\) common tha, is liye use bahar nikaal liya.

\(x = 400\) rakhein
\[400 = \dfrac{1}{2}(3u + 665)\]
\[800 = 3u + 665\]
\[3u = 135\]
\[u = \dfrac{135}{3} = 45 \text{ km/h}\]
Kyun: pehle dono taraf 2 se zarb diya taa ke \(\frac{1}{2}\) khatam ho (yeh qadam kitab chhod deti hai), phir 665 dono taraf se minus kiya, phir 3 se taqseem.

Hal (b): AB ka slope
Maan lijiye \(a\) pehle 3 ghante ka acceleration hai:
\[a = \text{slope of } \overline{AB} = \dfrac{|BF|}{|AF|} \quad \text{...(1)}\]
jahan \(|BF| = |BE| - |EF| = 70 - u = 70 - 45 = 25\) aur \(|AF| = |OE| = 3\).
Kyun: F, A ke barabar level par hai. To BF velocity ka barhna hai (\(u\) se 70 tak) aur AF guzra hua waqt (3 ghante). Rise taqseem run = slope = acceleration. (Kitab is equation ko bhi (1) number deti hai, ghabraiye nahin, yeh nayi equation hai.)

Values rakhein
\[a = \dfrac{25}{3} \approx 8.33 \text{ km/h}^{2}\]
Kyun: acceleration ki unit (km/h) har ghante mein, yani km/h\(^2\). Is ka matlab hai ke har ghante Ali ki raftaar taqreeban 8.33 km/h barhti rahi.

Tasdeeq:
\[\tfrac{1}{2}(45 + 70) \times 3 = 172.5\]
\[\tfrac{1}{2}(3 + 3.5) \times 70 = 227.5\]
\[172.5 + 227.5 = 400 \text{ km}\]
Poora 400 km aa gaya. Aur \(45 + \frac{25}{3} \times 3 = 70\) km/h, jo B par velocity hai.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Velocity-time graph mein \(v\) khari axis par aur \(t\) leti axis par hota hai.
2. Slope \(\frac{dv}{dt}\) = acceleration: leti line \(a = 0\), chadhti line \(a > 0\), girti line \(a < 0\) (retardation), curve = variable acceleration.
3. \(t_{1}\) se \(t_{2}\) tak graph ke neeche ka area \(= \int_{t_{1}}^{t_{2}} v\,dt\) = displacement.
4. Graph axis ke oopar aur neeche dono taraf ho: displacement \(= A_{1} - A_{2}\), distance \(= A_{1} + A_{2}\).
5. Area ko rectangles, triangles aur trapeziums mein todein; trapezium ka area \(= \frac{1}{2}(a + b)h\).
6. Hamesha units check karein aur jawab ko doosre tareeqe se tasdeeq karein.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Velocity-time graph ko displacement-time graph samajh lena: yahan leti line ka matlab constant velocity hai, "ruka hua" nahin.
2. Slope aur area ko ulat dena: slope se acceleration milta hai, area se displacement.
3. Displacement poocha ho aur \(A_{2}\) jama kar dena (ya distance poocha ho aur \(A_{2}\) minus kar dena).
4. Trapezium ki ghalat height lena: height do parallel sides ke darmiyan ka faasla hai (Example 6 ke BCDE mein 70, 0.5 nahin).
5. Units mix karna, maslan minutes ko m/s ke saath istemal karna.
6. Retardation ka sign: jawab "\(-\frac{3}{2}\) m/min\(^2\) acceleration" ya "\(\frac{3}{2}\) m/min\(^2\) deceleration" likhein, "\(-\frac{3}{2}\) deceleration" nahin (do minus mil kar ulta matlab de dete hain).
